questions.stem: A scientist reacts lead(II) nitrate solution with sodium bromide solution. This is the equation for the reaction. $\mathrm {P b} \left(\mathrm {N O} _ {3}\right) _ {2} (\mathrm {a q}) + 2 \mathrm {N a B r} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {P b B r} _ {2} (\mathrm {s}) + 2 \mathrm {N a N O} _ {3} (\mathrm {a q})$

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how the scientist could obtain a pure dry sample of lead(II) bromide $ \mathrm{(P b B r_{2})} $ from the reaction mixture.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The scientist reacts an excess of lead(II) nitrate solution with $ 2 5 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of sodium bromide solution of concentration $ 2. 0 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3}. $

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Show that the amount of sodium bromide used is 0.050 mol.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Show that the maximum theoretical mass of lead(II) bromide is approximately 9 g. [for $ \mathrm{P b B r}_{2} $ $ M_{\mathrm{r}}=3 6 7 $]

parts.label: c
parts.text: The scientist electrolyses molten lead(II) bromide using this apparatus.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Explain why lead(II) bromide needs to be molten rather than solid for electrolysis to occur.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: The electrolyte is at a temperature of $ 4 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ Explain a suitable material for the electrodes.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Give the half-equation that occurs at the negative electrode.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Bromine forms at the positive electrode. This is the half-equation for the reaction at the positive electrode. $2 \mathrm {B r} ^ {-} \rightarrow \mathrm {B r} _ {2} + 2 \mathrm {e} ^ {-}$

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: State what is observed at the positive electrode.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: State why the half-equation represents an oxidation reaction.
